key_highlights: ASX closed the week lower as traders priced in a potential fourth RBA rate hike, with house prices forecast to fall up to 10% on record
CBA reports home loan applications down 15% since the federal budget, signalling severe credit contraction in the housing market
Iron ore sector faces a structural shakeout masked by geopolitical conflict; Macarthur clears WA bulk test hurdle
ASIC launches review of whistleblower complaints at Big Four accounting firms, raising audit-quality concerns across ASX
Bathla's collapse exposes systemic fragility in Australia's construction sector, described as a 'Ponzi economy' symptom
Global AI momentum persists (Nvidia, Dell beats) but energy transition costs are mounting, pressuring Australian energy names
EV sales overtook petrol cars in Australia for the first time, driven by soaring fuel costs
Ratings agencies flag Victoria's soaring state debt as a credit risk
TMK Energy gas rates surge ahead of Mongolian drilling push; Beetaloo flagged to challenge gas cartel pricing

sectors.trend: Iron ore faces a hidden shakeout amid geopolitical conflict; small-cap miners (Kaoko, Vanadium, Piche, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals) showing relative strength. Macarthur clears WA bulk test. Gold remains supported by Netherlands repatriating 86t from US reserves.
sectors.implications: Large-cap miners (BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX) face margin pressure from iron ore demand softness. Small-cap exploration names offer speculative upside but carry elevated risk. Gold miners (GOLD.AX, NVG.AX) benefit from safe-haven flows.

sectors.trend: CBA flags 15% drop in home loan applications post-budget. Banks forecast record house price falls. CBA and Westpac face scrutiny over loyalty-customer pricing loopholes. ASIC audit review adds governance overhang.
sectors.implications: NIM compression risk as credit growth stalls. CBA.AX, WBC.AX, ANZ.AX, NAB.AX face earnings revision risk. REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) pressured by higher rates and falling property values.

sectors.trend: TMK Energy gas rates surge on Mongolian drilling. Beetaloo flagged to challenge gas cartel. Hydro Tasmania assesses record power request. Energy transition costs mounting. EV adoption accelerates, pressuring oil demand.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, BOQ.AX, SXG.AX benefit from gas pricing. Energy transition cost overhang pressures utilities (AGL.AX, CGP.AX). EV shift is a structural tailwind for lithium/energy-storage names.

sectors.trend: Bathla collapse exposes systemic fragility; described as symptomatic of a 'Ponzi economy'. Housing construction expected to follow prices lower. Melbourne councils admit inability to cope with planned population growth.
sectors.implications: Direct risk to construction names and materials suppliers. Broader signal of credit-cycle stress. Monitor GPT.AX, WBC.AX exposure to construction lending.

sectors.trend: Nvidia leads chip stocks higher; Dell posts monster quarterly beat on AI momentum. AI boom 'isn't over' per Nvidia. However, data centre backlash persists in Australia.
sectors.implications: Limited direct ASX exposure but positive for global tech sentiment. Australian data centre and cloud names (WES.AX, IAG.AX) may see indirect benefit. Local data centre opposition is a policy risk.

sectors.trend: EV sales overtake petrol cars. McDonald's value menu scarcity signals consumer cost pressure. Ozempic maker in trouble; tablet alternatives emerging. CSL remains a defensive anchor.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WOW.AX face margin pressure from input costs. CSL.AX, SGH.AX offer defensive stability. EV transition benefits battery and charging infrastructure plays.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure over the next 1–3 months as a fourth RBA rate hike looms and housing credit contraction deepens. CBA's 15% loan application drop is a leading indicator of a broader credit cycle turn. Iron ore weakness and construction contagion (Bathla) add downside risk. Offsetting positives: global AI momentum, gold strength, and gas pricing. Expect elevated volatility; ^AXJO likely to test lower supports.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook is cautiously constructive if the RBA pauses after a fourth hike and housing stabilises. The 'bull case returns' narrative suggests a cyclical recovery is possible, but Australia's stalling per-capita growth vs. Canada is a structural concern. Energy transition cost overhang and EV adoption create secular winners in gas, lithium, and charging infrastructure. Iron ore shakeout may create consolidation opportunities for well-capitalised miners. Construction sector will need a reset.
